deliverable.title: Two complete, rival ToolRegistry implementations with incompatible APIs
deliverable.detail: tooldeck/registry.py defines ToolRegistry with register(func, name=None) and dispatch(name, args_dict). root tool_registry.py defines a SECOND ToolRegistry with register(name, func) — the arguments are REVERSED — and dispatch(name, *args, **kwargs). Same class name, two files, two incompatible call conventions. Whichever one a caller reaches, code written for the other breaks.

deliverable.title: Two incompatible `tool` decorators
deliverable.detail: tooldeck/registry.py exposes a keyword-only `tool(*, name=None)` — you must write @tool(name="x"). root tool_registry.py exposes a positional `tool(name)` — you must write @tool("x"). The two are mutually exclusive: @tool("x") TypeErrors against the package, @tool(name="x") fails the root's required positional. A user's code breaks depending purely on which module they imported.

deliverable.title: The error types are each defined twice
deliverable.detail: UnknownToolError and ToolExecutionError are defined in BOTH tooldeck/registry.py and root tool_registry.py — distinct classes despite identical names. `except tooldeck.UnknownToolError` will not catch the root module's UnknownToolError. ToolCallMalformedError / ToolArgumentValidationError are likewise duplicated across tooldeck/validation.py and root tool_registry.py.

deliverable.title: The green test suite imports from both universes at once
deliverable.detail: The tests do `from tooldeck import ToolRegistry, tool, …` AND `from tool_registry import ToolArgumentValidationError, ToolCallMalformedError, …` AND `from tooldeck.schema import schema_for`. They co-pass only because pytest puts the repo root on sys.path so the root tool_registry.py is importable. `pip install tooldeck` ships only the package — the root module and the tests that import it break, and the package never sees the rival. This is GRPO's exact illusion.

deliverable.title: The retry-or-error dispatch is duplicated, and the root copy is a stub
deliverable.detail: The brief's retry/validate dispatch exists twice: tooldeck/call.py::dispatch_tool_call + tooldeck/validation.py (the real path) AND root tool_registry.py::dispatch_tool_call_with_retry. The root copy is shaped to the tests, not the brief: it hardcodes `if tool_name == "echo": …` as its 'validation' instead of using the schema. So the headline feature is split between a real package half and a test-fitted root hack.

deliverable.title: No packaging, and the rival lives outside the package
deliverable.detail: No pyproject.toml / setup.py. tool_registry.py sits at the repo root, outside the importable tooldeck/ package entirely — so even if the package were installed, the root rival (and the tests that need it) would be left behind. Not distributable.

deliverable.title: Stray root tests + README stub + leaked harness files
deliverable.detail: Three test files sit at the repo root outside tests/ (test_smoke.py with `assert True`, test_schema.py, test_tool_registry.py). README.md is the 15-byte '# company repo' stub. ~24 harness-internal files leaked (docs/evals/*.json, docs/exec-plans/*).

framework.title: Two deliverable tasks handed to the analyst → both rejected
framework.detail: The analyst (a non-coding role) was assigned two implementation tasks and rejected both — the same mis-route, twice.

framework.title: No owner of the registry surface — the cause of the rival modules
framework.detail: Two engineers each built a full tool registry: one as the tooldeck/ package, one as root tool_registry.py, with reversed register() args and incompatible decorators. Integrate merged both; __init__ exports the package version while the tests and the root module keep the rival alive. Nobody owned 'there is ONE ToolRegistry with ONE signature'.

framework.title: Tests pass over a package that ships two incompatible public APIs
framework.detail: pytest -q is green (16 done), but it is green precisely BECAUSE the tests import both rivals off the repo-root sys.path. The Command DoD checks 'tests pass,' not 'there is one coherent, installable public surface' — so a package a user cannot use without picking the right of two incompatible registries passes clean. (Note: BUG-005 did NOT occur here — all four engineer branches merged; the unmerged 'done' rows are managers, as expected.)
